sentences.en: RUTH: Ed, how are you getting on with the reading for our presentation next week?
sentences.zh: RUTH: Ed，下周我们演讲的阅读材料进展如何？

sentences.en: ED: Well, OK, Ruth - but there's so much of it.
sentences.zh: ED: 嗯，还行，Ruth——但材料实在太多了。

sentences.en: RUTH: know, I hadn't realised birth order was such a popular area of research.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 是啊，我之前没意识到出生顺序竟然是如此热门的研究领域。

sentences.en: ED: But the stuff on birth order and personality is mostly unreliable.
sentences.zh: ED: 但关于出生顺序与性格的研究大多并不可靠。

sentences.en: From what I've been reading a lot of the claims about how your position in the family determines certain personality traits are just stereotypes, with no robust evidence to support them.
sentences.zh: 据我所读，许多关于家庭中排行位置决定特定性格特质的说法，其实只是刻板印象，缺乏坚实证据支持。

sentences.en: RUTH: OK, but that's an interesting point - we could start by outlining what previous research has shown.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 好的，但这确实是个有趣的观点——我们可以先概述以往研究的发现。

sentences.en: There are studies going back over a hundred years.
sentences.zh: 相关研究可追溯至一百多年前。

sentences.en: ED: Yeah - so we could just run through some of the typical traits.
sentences.zh: ED: 没错——因此我们只需简要梳理一些典型特质。

sentences.en: Like the consensus seems to be that oldest children are generally less well-adjusted because they never get over the arrival of a younger sibling.
sentences.zh: 比如学界普遍认为，长子长女通常适应能力较差，因为他们始终无法真正接受弟弟妹妹的到来。

sentences.en: RUTH: Right, but on a positive note, some studies claimed that they were thought to be good at nurturing - certainly in the past when people had large families they would have been expected to look after the younger ones.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 没错，但换个积极角度看，有些研究声称他们被认为擅长养育照料——尤其在过去大家庭中，他们常被期望照看年幼的弟妹。

sentences.en: ED: There isn't such a clear picture for middle children - but one trait that a lot of the studies mention is that they is are easier to get on with than older or younger siblings.
sentences.zh: ED: 关于中间孩子，目前尚无清晰一致的结论——但多数研究都提到一个共同特质：他们比兄姐或弟妹更容易相处。

sentences.en: RUTH: Generally eager to please and helpful although that's certainly not accurate as far as my family goes - my middle brother a was a nightmare - always causing fights and envious of whatever I had.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 总体而言，他们通常渴望取悦他人且乐于助人；不过这点在我家显然不成立——我那位排行中间的哥哥简直就是个噩梦，总爱挑起争端，还嫉妒我拥有的一切。

sentences.en: ED: - As I said - none of this seems to relate tO my own experience.
sentences.zh: ED: ——正如我所说，这些说法似乎完全不符合我的亲身经历。

sentences.en: I'm the youngest in my family and don't recognise myself in any of the studies I've read about.
sentences.zh: 我是家中最小的孩子，但在所有我读过的相关研究中，却完全找不到自己的影子。

sentences.en: I'm supposed to have been a sociable and confident child who made friends easily - but I was actually terribly shy.
sentences.zh: 按理说我本该是个善于社交、自信满满、容易交朋友的孩子——可实际上我极度害羞。

sentences.en: RUTH: Really?
sentences.zh: RUTH: 真的吗？

sentences.en: That's funny.
sentences.zh: 这真有意思。

sentences.en: There have been hundreds of studies on twins but mostly about nurture versus nature
sentences.zh: 关于双胞胎的研究已有数百项，但大多聚焦于教养与天性之争。

sentences.en: ED: There was one on personality, which said that a twin is likely to be quite shy in social situations because they always have their twin around to depend on for support.
sentences.zh: ED: 其中有一项关于性格的研究指出，双胞胎在社交场合往往相当害羞，因为他们总能依赖身旁的孪生兄弟或姐妹提供支持。

sentences.en: RUTH: My cousins were like that when they were small - they were only interested in each other and found it hard to engage with other kids.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 我表亲小时候就是那样——他们只对彼此感兴趣，很难与其他孩子互动。

sentences.en: They're fine now though.
sentences.zh: 不过现在他们已经完全没问题了。

sentences.en: ED: Only children have had a really bad a press - a lot of studies have branded them as loners who think the world revolves around them because they've never had to fight for their parents' attention.
sentences.zh: ED: 独生子女一直饱受负面评价——大量研究将他们贴上‘孤僻者’的标签，称他们自以为世界围着自己转，因为从未需要争夺父母的关注。

sentences.en: RUTH: That does seem a bit harsh.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 这听起来确实有点苛刻。

sentences.en: One category I hadn't considered before was children with much older siblings - couple of studies mentioned that these children grow up more quickly and are expected to do basic things for themselves - like getting dressed.
sentences.zh: 此前我未曾考虑过的一类孩子是：有年龄大得多的兄姐者。有几项研究提到，这类孩子成长速度更快，且被期待能独立完成基本事务，例如自己穿衣。

sentences.en: ED: can see how that might be true - although I expect they're sometimes the exact opposite playing the baby role and clamouring for special treatment.
sentences.zh: ED: 我能理解这可能属实——不过我想他们有时恰恰相反，反而刻意扮演婴儿角色，极力索求特殊待遇。

sentences.en: RUTH: What was the problem with most of these studies, do you think?
sentences.zh: RUTH: 你觉得这些研究最主要的问题出在哪里？

sentences.en: ED: think it was because in a lot of cases data was collected from only one sibling per family, who rated him or herself and his or her siblings at the same time.
sentences.zh: ED: 我认为问题在于，许多情况下数据仅来自每个家庭中的一名子女，由其同时对自己及兄弟姐妹进行自我评估。

sentences.en: RUTH: Mmm.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 嗯。

sentences.en: Some of the old research into the relationship between birth order and academic achievement has been proved to be accurate though.
sentences.zh: 不过，过去有关出生顺序与学业成就关系的部分研究已被证实是准确的。

sentences.en: Performances in intelligence tests decline slightly from the eldest child to his or her younger siblings.
sentences.zh: 智力测试成绩会从长子长女开始，向其弟妹略微递减。

sentences.en: This has been proved in lots of recent studies.
sentences.zh: 这一点已在众多近期研究中得到验证。

sentences.en: ED: Yes.
sentences.zh: ED: 是的。

sentences.en: Although what many of them didn't take into consideration was family size.
sentences.zh: 尽管其中许多研究未将家庭规模纳入考量。

sentences.en: The more siblings there are, the likelier the family is to have low socio- economic status - which can also account for differences between siblings in academic performance.
sentences.zh: 兄弟姐妹越多，家庭社会经济地位偏低的可能性就越大——这也同样可解释兄弟姐妹间学业表现的差异。

sentences.en: RUTH: The oldest boy might be given more opportunities than his younger sisters, for example.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 例如，长子可能比他的妹妹们获得更多机会。

sentences.en: ED: Exactly.
sentences.zh: ED: 没错。

sentences.en: RUTH: But the main reason for the marginally higher academic performance of oldest iS children is quite surprising, I think.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 但长子长女学业表现略优的主要原因，我觉得还挺令人意外的。

sentences.en: It's not only that they benefit intellectually from extra attention at a young age which is what I would have expected.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是因为他们在幼年时获得了更多智力层面的关注——而这正是我原本所预期的。

sentences.en: It's that they benefit from being teachers for their younger siblings, by verbalising processes.
sentences.zh: 更关键的是，他们通过向弟妹讲解过程（即语言化表达），扮演了‘小老师’的角色，从而获益。

sentences.en: ED: Right, and this gives them status and confidence, which again contribute, in a small way, to better performance.
sentences.zh: ED: 对，这赋予了他们地位感和自信心，而这两者又以微小的方式促成了更佳的学业表现。

sentences.en: So would you say sibling rivalry has been a useful thing for you?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得兄弟姐妹之间的竞争对你来说是一件有益的事情吗？

sentences.en: RUTH: think so - my younger brother was incredibly annoying and we fought a lot but l think this has made me a stronger person.
sentences.zh: RUTH: 我觉得是——我弟弟小的时候特别讨厌，我们经常吵架，但我觉得这让我变成了一个更坚强的人。

sentences.en: I know how to defend myself.
sentences.zh: 我知道如何保护自己。

sentences.en: We had / some terrible arguments and I would have died rather than apologise to him - but we had to put up with each other and most of the time we co-existed amicably / enough.
sentences.zh: 我们曾有过一些非常激烈的争吵，我宁死也不愿向他道歉——但我们又不得不彼此忍受，而且大多数时候我们相处得还算融洽。

sentences.en: ED: Yes, my situation was pretty similar.
sentences.zh: ED: 是的，我的情况也差不多。

sentences.en: But I don't think having two older brothers made me any less selfish - I was never prepared to let my brothers use any of my stuff
sentences.zh: 但我并不认为有两个哥哥就让我变得不那么自私了——我从来都不愿意让哥哥们用我的任何东西。

sentences.en: RUTH: That's perfectly normal, whereas .
sentences.zh: RUTH: 这完全正常，而……
